Through pilots, the project will identify opportunities for international, including UK, companies to partner with Chinese counterparts to deliver major projects, also laying the groundwork for the Infrastructure pillar of the China prosperity programme.

titles: Supporting China's ability to monitor climate risks and develop climate infrastructure, helping work towards a lower carbon society.
descriptions: This project is designed to define a set of climate risk indicators that provide Chinese decision-makers with a clearer picture of climate risk. This will help to develop China's markets in climate resilient infrastructure and insurance, supporting China's move to a lower carbon society. China is the world's largest emitter of greenhouse gasses and largest energy consumer and producer. This project will lay groundwork for the Energy and Low Carbon pillar of a China prosperity programme which will look to match China's specific reform needs with energy and low carbon sector strengths, reducing global emissions by accelerating China's energy transition.

titles: Scoping study to analyse gas infrastructure access and opportunities around pricing regulations reform in China
descriptions: This project will scope activity on natural gas market reforms in China for the Low Carbon and Energy pillar of the forthcoming multiyear China Phase One prosperity programme. It seeks to research China's prioritisation of reforms and support the removal of the main barriers hindering China's attempt to increase the share of natural gas in its energy mix. By pursuing prosperity partnerships, it is also expected to generate opportunities for international business, including UK companies.

titles: Supporting power sector reform in South China to increase integration of renewable energy into the region.
descriptions: This project is designed to support China's adoption of new market arrangements in its power sector to enable the effective integration of renewable energy. Building on a previous project, it will draw upon UK policy and market expertise to inform and accelerate Yunnan's power market reforms and create new bilateral partnerships in key reform pilots, including in Chongqing and Guangdong. It is expected that the market structure decisions taken by China will generate commercial opportunities for international business, including from UK. This project will further set groundwork for the Energy/Low Carbon pillar of a China prosperity programme, which will match China's specific reform needs with energy and low carbon sector strengths, reducing global emissions by accelerating China's energy transition.

This project will lay groundwork for the Infrastructure pillar of the forthcoming China prosperity programme. This pillar will promote the involvement of international best practice in design, engineering, financial, professional and legal services, and environmental and social standards in growth enhancing Chinese led projects.

titles: The project will research the development of the New Energy Vehicle industry in China
descriptions: This project is designed to respond to high Chinese demand for collaboration on New Energy Vehicle (NEV) policies, research and commercial opportunities. The programme will match China's specific reform needs with energy and low carbon sector strengths, reducing global emissions by accelerating China's energy transition.

titles: Supporting reform of the power sector in China

titles: Supporting China's development of its regulatory approach to financial innovation

This is intended to build Chinese capacity, support innovation, improve efficiency and manage risks. It will support the building of a more robust financial system in China. It will also provide a platform for the Financial Services pillar of a China prosperity programme. This pillar will work to promote financial sector reform though sharing policy and private sector expertise, and capacity building in the Chinese regulatory sector, to enable a transition to a more innovative and inclusive economy. This will also work to generate opportunities for international business, bringing benefits to British business in sectors where they are well placed to compete, including; Rule of Law, Energy and Low Carbon, Financial Services and Infrastructure.

titles: Promoting China’s Alignment with International Standards for Animal Testing.
descriptions: The project seeks to reform China’s animal testing laws, associated regulations and codes, aligning them and Chinese industries’ practice with internationally-recognised standards, including the reduction of unnecessary animal testing in cosmetics and pharmaceuticals. This will help China’s science policy to develop towards a more open environment for international innovation collaboration, in sectors which will drive future economic growth. This will also facilitate the removal of trade barriers, thus generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting international participation in China's bond and equities market
descriptions: This project is designed to support the development of China's bond market by enhancing its audit regulatory framework. It will promote and enhance cooperation between China and global financial markets, which will support the international issuance of Chinese Yuan Renminbi (RMB)-denominated bonds in China. This collaboration will support the opening up of China's bond market to international participants, and support sustainable economic growth in China. The project is a foundation for the Financial Services pillar of a China prosperity programme. This pillar will work to promote financial sector reform though sharing policy and private sector expertise, and capacity building in the Chinese regulatory sector, to enable a transition to a more efficient, productive, inclusive economy.

titles: Financial Conduct Regulation: UK Principles, Experience and Implications for China
descriptions: This project will develop and deliver a pilot training programme on financial conduct regulation with UK best practice. There are significant risks in the Chinese financial system and there is a pressing need to enhance regulatory capacity and frameworks to ensure the stability and sustainability of the Chinese financial system. This is not only of critical importance to China's domestic economy it is also of key interest to the global economy. The project is a foundation for the Financial Services pillar of a China prosperity programme. This pillar will work to promote financial sector reform though sharing policy and private sector expertise, and capacity building in the Chinese regulatory sector, to enable a transition to a more efficient, productive, inclusive economy.

titles: Enhancing regulatory effectiveness for business in China
descriptions: This project is designed to enhance the effectiveness of regulations for business in China. It will introduce UK best practice and support China's creation of a robust regulatory regime that will enhance the sustainability of its financial system. This will reduce financial risks and market misconduct thereby benefiting international including UK business' in China. The project will lay the foundations for the Rule of Law pillar of a China prosperity programme. This pillar will support China's progress towards a stronger rule of law including clearer judicial processes, dispute resolution and protection of intellectual property, ultimately leading to an improved business environment and stronger economic growth.

titles: Designing a measurement tool to evaluate the impact of the Rule of Law for Business programme in China
descriptions: This project aims to establish a monitoring and evaluation tool with core indicators of success to assess the progress and impact of the Rule of Law for Business programme. The programme will support China's progress on the rule of law for business including clearer judicial processes, commercial dispute resolution and protection of intellectual property, leading to an improved business environment and stronger economic growth. It is also expected to generate opportunities for international business, bringing benefits to British business in sectors where they are well placed to compete, including; Rule of Law, Energy and Low Carbon, Financial Services and Infrastructure.
